A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Thread for retrieval-augmented how-to question answering. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and corresponding content can be matched across the extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mind2Web and WikiHow experiments, incident-mitigation evaluations with 19 retained on-call engineers, and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original evaluations across all three scenarios and adds reported experiments using LLaMA3-70B on WikiHow.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the five LU components, four LU types, optional document reformulation, extraction/merging/update procedures, and header retrieval, prerequisite selection, and linker-guided iteration. The retained appendix prompts describe the same core procedure; the removed multi-agent study concerns an auxiliary system variant.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Mind2Web Cross-Task web navigation, Microsoft-product WikiHow instructions, and simple and hard incident-mitigation cases. The document-format scenarios also remain. The added backbone experiment uses existing WikiHow coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds chunk-based RAG to the reported single-turn WikiHow comparison, with SR 19.59; v1 Table 3 explicitly omitted this comparator because retrieval was inadequate. The main Mind2Web and data-organization comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 Section 5.5 adds a WikiHow evaluation using LLaMA3-70B alongside GPT-4. The auxiliary single-agent versus multi-agent evaluation setting from v1 Appendix E.4 is removed. Retained experiments preserve their dataset sizes, splits, metrics, retrieval settings, and GPT configurations.

E4.justification: v2 adds backbone sensitivity analysis across Chunk, Doc, and Thread, but removes v1's multi-agent ablation and the GPT-3.5 portion of the chat-history ablation. The GPT-4 history comparison moves from v1 Table 14 into v2 Table 5; selector and document-format analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Both retain temperature 0, top_p 1, and randomized baseline ordering in the engineer study. The added backbone results also use point estimates.

E6.justification: Retained main results match, including the incident-mitigation chart and its replacement table at plotted precision. New results include single-turn Chunk scores of 19.59 SR, 60.20 precision, 25.16 recall, and 35.49 F1, plus LLaMA3-70B Thread scores of 60.82 SR and 72.84 F1. v2 removes the multi-agent result with SR 15.66 and GPT-3.5 no-history results, and adds the 79.90 Op. F1 diagnostic for always predicting CLICK.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems, or proofs. The descriptive LU and how-to categories retain their meaning, and the displayed precision and recall formulas are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim that Thread improves how-to QA through interconnected logic units remains. v2 elevates resource efficiency to a headline contribution, explicitly claiming reduced knowledge-base size and generation-context requirements in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. These claims largely summarize measurements already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the LLaMA3 results as evidence that Thread narrows the backbone performance gap and generalizes across LLMs. Its limitations accordingly describe ChatGPT and LLaMA coverage, while v1's interpretation of multi-agent benefits disappears. The limitations concerning untested factoid questions and initial LU-extraction costs remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address and explicitly clarifies that chunk and LU selection use the same LLM-based selection strategy in Appendix C.1, footnote 12. Most construction, selection, evaluation, and generation prompts, along with chunk sizes, overlaps, retrieval depths, and decoding settings, are retained through the appendix reorganization.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Allam and Haggag (2012), Deng et al. (2023b), and Yang et al. (2018), while removing several background and multi-agent references, including Bolotova et al. (2022), Krishna et al. (2021), and Wu et al. (2023). Section 2 largely preserves the positioning against chunk-based and knowledge-graph organization.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, replacing much of the philosophical and taxonomy-led opening with a direct problem statement and explicit contribution list. Main-result discussion is reordered, appendix sections are consolidated, limitations move to Appendix E, and the separate ethics statement is removed.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 becomes a branching troubleshooting example, Figure 2 gains a concrete LU illustration, and the incident-mitigation chart becomes Table 3. v2 also adds the backbone chart, combines history and selector ablations, and reformats appendix prompts into shaded blocks.

improvement.justification: The single-turn Chunk results complete a previously omitted comparison, and the LLaMA3 experiment partly addresses v1's explicit limitation concerning reliance on OpenAI models. The expanded LU construction figure and tabulated incident results make the method and evidence easier to inspect. Removing the multi-agent and GPT-3.5 history ablations loses supplementary evidence, but the gains in evaluating and explaining the central Thread contribution support a limited net improvement.
